evidence: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/components/embeddable-host.hbs:9-10,16-17 render icon-only d-buttons with no label/title; d-button.js.es6 only sets the title attribute from `title` or `label`, so these buttons get no accessible name. Other admin templates do pass title= for icon buttons (backups_index.hbs:24,27). The claim that the keys don't exist is only partly right: client.en.yml:2498 already defines admin.embedding.edit. This is a low-impact accessibility improvement.

store.js.es6:196-200 calls obj[k].map without a guard whenever a key matches /_ids$/. The only producer in this PR is EmbeddingSerializer (has_many ... embed: :ids), which always emits an array ([] when empty), so the crash can't happen with current server output. It would only happen if some other serializer emitted a null *_ids. Separately, `hydrated || []` is dead code because map always returns an array. A defensive guard is cheap, but this is not a live bug.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-11 and 15-17: where(id:).first returns nil for an unknown id, and then save_host (host.host=) or host.destroy raises NoMethodError, giving a 500 instead of a 404. The endpoint is admin-only, so impact is low. Fix: use EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]) (RecordNotFound -> 404) or find_by with an explicit not-found response.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 requires the TLD to be `\.[a-z]{2,5}`, so hosts like example.museum or blog.community (and localhost) fail validation. The old site setting had no such restriction, so this is a regression for those users. Loosen it to {2,63} or validate via URI parsing.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8 calls self.host.sub! unconditionally in before_validation. EmbeddableHost.new.valid?, or a create/update request without embeddable_host[:host] (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 assigns params[...][:host], which can be nil), raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` or use safe navigation. (sub! also mutates the caller's params string in place.)

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-16 indexes [0] on PG::Result from both queries. site_settings only holds rows for overridden settings, so on a fresh install or any site that never set embed_category, the first query returns 0 rows and PG::Result#[0] raises IndexError, aborting the migration. The uncategorized_category_id fallback has the same problem when that row is absent (migrations run before seeds). Check ntuples/cmd_tuples first, as the embeddable_hosts block at lines 18-19 already does.

Same migration, line 25: '#{h}' is interpolated straight into an INSERT. A host value containing a quote breaks the migration, and it is a SQL injection pattern even though the data is admin-supplied. val.split("\n") also leaves blank or \r-suffixed entries, which get inserted as-is. Use connection.quote(h.strip) and skip blank entries.

spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:17-27 is the private_category fabricator moved byte-for-byte from the base category_fabricator.rb (the PR swapped the two files' contents). update! in after_build and transients[:group].id are pre-existing behavior, not introduced here. Every caller passes group: (guardian_spec.rb:278, invite_spec.rb:132, topics_controller_spec.rb:757, topic_spec.rb:1455, posts_controller_spec.rb:840), and none use Fabricate.build. Technically true but out of scope for this PR. The real smell is the swapped filenames (category fabricators now live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and vice versa).

The repo has no .rubocop.yml at this revision, so no Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody rule is enforced. Blank lines after `describe ... do` and before `end` are the prevailing Discourse spec style (e.g. spec/controllers/admin/*_spec.rb, spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb follow existing files).
spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1407 `describe 'with an emeddable host'` was introduced in this PR (not present at base 913c3d6). It's a trivial typo in a test description with no functional impact.

test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:111 calls store.find('fruit', 2), but create-pretender.js.es6:226-228 always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]). Banana (id 2) has color_ids [3], so the assertions for colors [1,2] only pass because the mock ignores the id. The test is misleading. Either request fruit 1, or make the mock look up by request.params.id and assert banana's colors.
